title: Panthers vs. Saints Preview: Expert Predictions, Spread Pick & Odds from Action Network
body:
The Carolina Panthers and the New Orleans Saints, both sitting at 3‑5 on the NFL ladder, will clash Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in a pivotal Week 10 matchup at the Caesars Superdome. With identical records and a shared need to climb out of the lower half of the conference, the game carries added weight for playoff‑hopefuls and teams looking to salvage a season. Broadcast on FOX, the contest offers a rare glimpse of two struggling franchises trying to assert dominance in the NFC South, while also providing a testing ground for emerging talent on both sides of the ball.

For the Panthers, the spotlight falls on quarterback Bryce Young, who entered the season with lofty expectations after being selected first overall. Young’s early struggles have been evident in a 2‑4 start as a starter, but the past two weeks have shown flashes of the poise that made him a top prospect. In the most recent win against the New York Giants, Young posted a 300‑yard passing effort and two touchdowns, demonstrating an improved command of the offense. Yet his consistency remains in question; he still throws a high number of interceptions per game and has yet to establish a reliable rhythm with his receiving corps. The Panthers’ ground game, anchored by veteran running back Chuba Hubbard and the versatile D’Onta Foreman, has been modest, averaging just over three yards per carry. To keep the Saints off balance, Carolina will need to blend short, high‑percentage passes with occasional deep shots to stretch New Orleans’ secondary, which has given up a league‑average 7.1 yards per reception.

New Orleans, meanwhile, is grappling with the aftermath of a quarterback carousel that saw Derek Carr and Jameis Winston share snaps before the team settled on Carr for the remainder of the season. Carr’s veteran presence has steadied the offense, but his numbers are far from spectacular—he’s posted a 67.5 passer rating and a 2‑4 record as a starter. The Saints’ true strength lies in their play‑action scheme, orchestrated by offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr., which leverages the speed of wideout Chris Olave and the reliability of tight end Juwan Johnson. Olave, who has already eclipsed 800 receiving yards, remains the focal point of the attack, and his ability to gain yards after the catch will be critical against a Panthers defense that has allowed 24.3 points per game, the fourth‑most in the league.

Defensively, both squads are in the midst of rebuilding phases. Carolina’s secondary, anchored by rookie cornerback Jaycee Horn, has been porous, surrendering a passer rating of 115.9 to opposing quarterbacks. The Panthers rely heavily on an aggressive pass rush led by Brian Burns and the emerging pass‑rusher DJ Moore, yet they have generated only 2.8 sacks per game. New Orleans, on the other hand, boasts a more seasoned front seven. Defensive end Cameron Jordan continues to be a disruptive force, while linebacker Demario Davis provides leadership against the run. The Saints have limited opponents to a 3.9‑yard rushing average, a statistic that could force the Panthers to become one‑dimensional if they cannot establish the run.

Special teams could also swing momentum. The Panthers’ rookie kicker, Zane Gonzalez, has struggled with consistency, missing three of his last five attempts from inside 40 yards. Conversely, New Orleans’ veteran kicker, Wil Lutz, is 13‑for‑13 on field goals of 40 yards or less this season, making the Saints’ extra points a near‑certainty. A missed field goal or a blocked punt in a low‑scoring affair could prove decisive, especially given the historical trend of close games between the two rivals.

Looking ahead, the outcome of this contest will likely dictate the trajectory of each franchise’s season. A Panthers victory would not only break a three‑game losing streak but also provide a morale boost ahead of a challenging stretch that includes trips to Dallas and Seattle. For the Saints, a win would reaffirm Derek Carr’s role as the team’s quarterback of the future and keep them within striking distance of the NFC South’s top spot, still occupied by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As both teams seek to rewrite their narratives, Sunday’s showdown promises a blend of strategic adjustments, individual performances, and the ever‑present quest for a much‑needed win.
